chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub said: Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Ali ibn Hassaan, from Abdurrahman ibn Katheer, from al-Mufadhdhal ibn Umar, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying:

The man of this matter has two occultations. In one of them, he returns to his family, and in the other it is said: 'He has perished,' (or) 'in which valley he has followed.' I said: 'What shall we do if that happens?' He said: 'If a claimant claims, ask him about those great matters, in which only he (the true one) will answer.'

Allah would not leave the believers in the condition which you are in until He separates the evil from the good; nor is Allah going to make you acquainted with the unseen, but Allah chooses from His messengers whom He pleases. So believe in Allah and His messengers. And if you believe and fear Allah, then for you is a great reward.

These traditions mention that the Qa'im (peace be upon him) disappears twice. Allah confirmed the sayings of the Infallible Imams (peace be upon them). The first disappearance was the one during which the deputies between Imam al-Mahdi (may Allah hasten his return) and the people were apparent in persons and positions. Through them, obscure matters of knowledge and clear judgments were clarified. All questions and issues raised were answered by them. This was the short disappearance, whose time has elapsed. In the second disappearance, there were no deputies or mediators. It was Allah's will to test His people and distinguish them after letting confusion spread among them. Allah said: 'Allah will not leave the believers in the condition which you are in until He separates the evil from the good, and He will not make you acquainted with the unseen.' The second disappearance has taken place. We ask Allah to make us among those who remain firm on the truth and do not slip away after the trials. This is what is meant by 'two occultations' or 'he disappears twice'.

key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْأَمْرِ: the master of the affair (referring to Imam al-Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: What are the two occultations of Imam al-Mahdi and how do they differ?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* outlines the doctrine of the two occultations of Imam al-Mahdi, distinguishing the Minor Occultation (*al-Ghayba al-Sughra*) characterized by specific deputies, from the Major Occultation (*al-Ghayba al-Kubra*) marked by general waiting. It provides the criterion for distinguishing the true Imam from pretenders (*da'wan*) through their knowledge of esoteric truths, while citing Quranic verses to emphasize that divine testing involves concealing the unseen until the appointed time.
